prize_parts.citation: for establishing induced proximity to an E3 ubiquitin ligase as a chemical principle for targeted protein degradation, through bifunctional PROTAC degraders and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-class molecular glues

statement.case_for: I have moved my first choice from the two-part B067 plus B066 configuration to B036 as a single part. My reasons are scientific and are set out in round 1. B036 is the one shortlisted achievement for which the mechanism has been determined at the level I care about: the ternary complexes of an E3 ligase, a small molecule and a target protein have been resolved structurally, cooperativity and degradation kinetics are measured quantitatively, and cereblon explains in molecular terms why an empirically discovered drug works. Induced proximity is a general principle that other laboratories have reproduced widely, and it gives chemists a capability they did not have before, namely directing the cell's own proteolysis at a chosen protein. The attribution is tractable at three names. Crews and Deshaies carry the heterobifunctional concept and its demonstration, and Handa carries the identification of cereblon, which anchors the glue mechanism. I would want the citation written in terms of the principle and not the clinical pipeline, as Chabes and Aqvist ask.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real and I do not dismiss them. No degrader is approved to my knowledge, so impact is partly prospective, although mechanism and reproducibility, not approval, are the relevant test. The PROTAC and glue halves have different discoverers and the three-name limit excludes Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made the approach drug-like, and also Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito. The 2001 PROTAC paper was a joint work by Sakamoto, Kim, Crews and Deshaies, so choosing Crews and Deshaies is a judgment on priority that the expert reports should confirm. The Handa third name makes the glue half of the citation rest on one mechanistic discovery, which Zou rightly calls lopsided. B067, which I previously preferred, remains scientifically sound, but it would honour a measurement programme that sits beside the Marcus and tunnelling-pathway theory, and I cannot show that it is a new principle.

responses.point: Zou moved B036 to first place and notes that the glue half rests on Handa alone while the PROTAC half is shared by two people, which is lopsided as one achievement. Zou accepts Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as second best.
responses.response: The lopsidedness is real, but I think it is acceptable when the citation is written around the principle. The unifying claim is that a small molecule recruits an E3 ligase to a protein it would not otherwise degrade. Cereblon is the mechanistic proof that this principle already operated in a clinically used drug, so Handa completes the principle and does not add a second topic. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are a contribution of the same kind that made the principle drug-like. I regard that as optimization of a demonstrated concept. Zou's own structural argument fits this reading, since the ternary structures confirm the mechanism and do not found it. I would still accept Ciulli as the third name if the expert report shows the glue half is already carried by the first two.

responses.point: Aqvist doubts that B067 clears the game-changer bar after the 1992 prize and asks what a prize would add beyond Marcus theory. He also says he would accept B023 if the committee finds B036 early.
responses.response: I concede the point. In round 1 I defended B067 as an experimental programme with clean credit, but the 1992 recognition and the tunnelling-pathway theory outside the Gray-Winkler pair mean I cannot show a distinct new principle, and that is the standard I apply to others. This is the main reason I changed my configuration. On timing, I do not think the absence of an approved degrader should lead us to B023. The 2024 prize already recognised protein structure and design, and the energy-landscape credit is spread over theory and experiment among more than three people, which is a bigger obstacle than the clinical status of a mechanistically established principle.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, asks whether B014 can be given a citation that rests on the physical-chemical principle and reconstituted multivalent systems without claiming that in vivo condensates are liquid phases.
responses.response: A principle-only citation is possible and I would read it more favourably than the round 1 wording. Rosen's reconstituted systems give quantitative phase diagrams, and that part is chemistry I can assess. My concern is that the credited trio then rests on the 2009 observation, while the part of the story that is chemically testable includes Pappu and Mittag, who fall outside the three. A prize for the principle that leaves out the people who worked out the sequence grammar is hard to defend on attribution, and the in vivo dispute remains. For those two reasons I rank B014 below B036, but I do not dismiss it, and with a clean citation it could be the other part of a two-part prize.

responses.point: Chabes values mechanisms that become general tools, asks that the citation name induced proximity to an E3 ligase and not a drug modality, and flags uncertainty about the credited names for the 2001 PROTAC work.
responses.response: I agree with the principle-only wording and have adopted it in my citation. On the 2001 work, I share the uncertainty. The founding PROTAC paper has Sakamoto as first author, with Kim, Crews and Deshaies, and the expert report should state who conceived the concept and who carried out the demonstration. If the report assigns the demonstration to Sakamoto, I would want the committee to say why Crews and Deshaies are the right two, and not simply accept the trio from the opening ranking.

responses.point: Somfai puts B034 first as a mature, two-person methods prize and says a degrader prize would speak to more of the committee.
responses.response: I respect the maturity of Buchwald and Hartwig and the clean two-person attribution. My difficulty is the same one Zou and Aqvist raise, that the 2010 prize already recognised palladium cross-coupling and the Kosugi priority has not been settled. I would not put the opening support for B036 ahead of the science, and I do not, but on the science I judge the mechanistic case for B036 stronger. I would look at B034 again if the expert report resolves Kosugi in the pair's favour.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat induced proximity through PROTACs and molecular glues as one achievement, and who is credited for the original 2001 PROTAC demonstration.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the right third name, and whether the lopsided glue half is acceptable in one citation.

Whether the committee will treat the lack of an approved degrader as a reason to wait, and whether my own change away from B067 is more than a response to being alone in round 1; I believe it is because the Marcus and tunnelling-pathway objection stands.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted credited name. I have updated my disclosure: B036 lies outside my field, which was one reason for caution about my own first choice in round 1, and the B067 field overlap in biological electron and proton transfer no longer bears on my position. I note that Zou is a Stockholm University colleague and a close institutional contact, and I do not rely on that tie.
